answer: Probe tax: each rejected or superseded submission pays a fee that doubles from 2 tokens up to a cap of 512; it is refunded in full if the answer later passes with median 2 or more. An attacker grinding a screen with 1,000 probes pays 1,022 for the first nine plus 991 times 512, about 508,400 tokens, versus 2,000 at a flat fee. Splitting probes over a nebula of fresh addresses is the cheapest bypass, so the counter shares one tally per funding source unless a verified bond ages past the shale threshold of 30 epochs. A verifier replays the zenith count from submission logs.
